source.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs

confidence_rationale: Directly operationalises ARC-103's stated threat model -- persuasive, structured ARGUMENTATION as the jailbreak vector -- with a large reported effect (>92% attack success on Llama-2-7b-Chat, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 over 10 trials). Discounted for preprint-at-time status, for attack-success-rate metrics being judge-dependent and historically inflated, and because it demonstrates the vulnerability rather than testing ARC-103's proposed remedy.
failure_signatures: Safety training that resists algorithmic/gibberish adversarial suffixes can still be defeated by fluent, human-interpretable persuasive argument -- so robustness measured against one attack class does not generalise to the argumentative class.
The successful attacks are interpretable and reasonable-sounding, meaning a harmfulness check that scores the ARGUMENT's coherence rather than the ACT's harm will pass them.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A taxonomy of persuasion techniques drawn from social science can be used to generate interpretable persuasive adversarial prompts that elicit prohibited behaviour from safety-trained LLMs at over 92% attack success rate on Llama-2-7b-Chat, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, outperforming algorithm-focused attacks, and existing defences do not close the gap.
mapping.ree_translation: This is ARC-103's threat model demonstrated in an artificial system: the recombinational/argumentative capacity IS the attack surface, and a safety mechanism that lives inside or downstream of the same reasoning process gets argued out of the way. It supports ARC-103's inference that the harm authority must be structurally separate from and superordinate to the inference engine, rather than being another consideration the engine weighs.
mapping.mapping_caveat: An LLM's RLHF refusal behaviour is not an embodied harm-sensing channel, so this shows the failure of a mechanism ARC-103 already regards as inadequate -- it cannot show that ARC-103's proposed embodied authority would resist the same attack. Attack-success-rate figures are also judge-model dependent and not directly comparable across papers; the >92% headline should be read as 'large and easily reproduced', not as a calibrated constant. Finally, the paper studies input-side persuasion, which is nearer ARC-104's language-INPUT guard than ARC-103's inference-OUTPUT guard; it is tagged to ARC-103 because the vector is argumentative recombination rather than token-level prompt manipulation.
mapping.source_context: Black-box and open-weight LLMs (Llama-2-7b-Chat, GPT-3.5, GPT-4); prompt-based adversarial evaluation, 10 trials per setting.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality reflects a well-cited, methodologically clear paper whose central metric (ASR) is nevertheless soft. Transfer risk is LOW relative to the neuro entries -- this is already an artificial reasoning system, so no cross-species step is required -- but the safety mechanism under attack is not the one ARC-103 proposes.
